title: Hands-on JavaScript SDK mini tutorial + debugging notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact, hands-on walkthrough for engineers who need a fast path to integrate Redwood's JavaScript SDK into a prototype or demo app. Focus is: minimal install, local dev flow, sanity checks, common failure modes and quick debug commands. NOT a full reference — link to README and API docs for exhaustive detail.

Audience:
- Frontend engineers building prototypes (React / Next.js)
- Backend engineers adding small LLM endpoints (Node/Express, Fastify)
- SDK adopters who want sample code + troubleshooting in one place

Scope / assumptions:
- Node 18+ or modern browser environment (ES modules supported)
- dev env has RW_API_KEY for hosted runs (or local stub for offline)
- Using stable sdk-js package (see linked PR for ongoing changes)

Quickstart (5–7 minute path):
1) npm/yarn — install
   - npm install @redwood/inference-js --save
2) Minimal example (Node):
   - create index.js with this minimal usage:

   const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-js');
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY });

   async function run() {
     const out = await client.generate({
       model: 'redwood-alpha-1',
       prompt: 'Summarize the main point of: "Make things simple"',
       maxTokens: 80
     });
     console.log(out.text || out.choices?.[0]?.text);
   }

   run().catch(err => {
     console.error('run failed:', err.message);
     process.exit(1);
   });

3) Environment and secrets:
   - export RW_API_KEY=xxx (local) or use .env in dev. For browsers use short-lived tokens via backend proxy (do NOT embed production keys).

4) Run and validate:
   - node index.js -> expect textual output within 500ms-2s depending on model.
   - If blank: enable verbose logging (client.config.log = true) or inspect network call in devtools.

Minimal React example (client-side streaming pattern):
- High-level pattern: auth via backend -> open streaming request -> render chunks as they arrive. Use AbortController for cancellation. See sample in README for event-stream handling.

Common errors and fast fixes:
- 401 / invalid API key: verify env var name; confirm token not expired. For short-lived tokens, ensure backend minting works (check server time skew).
- CORS blocked in browser: user called hosted API directly with full API key (bad). Fix: proxy request through backend or use token exchange flow.
- Rate limit 429: retry with exponential backoff (Jitter + limit up to 3 attempts). Consider switching to a smaller model or reduce client-side concurrency.
- Slow responses / timeouts: check model choice vs sequence length. For streaming, ensure client handles partial chunks rather than waiting for final payload.
- Unexpected shape (no text field): server may be returning delta-streams; look for choices vs text top-level fields. Use helper client.format() in SDK to normalize.

Debugging checklist (local):
- Is RW_API_KEY present? echo $RW_API_KEY 
- Can I curl the endpoint used by SDK? curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_API_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Enable SDK debug: process.env.RW_SDK_DEBUG=1 (prints request ids, latencies, errors)\- If streaming, use Node with --experimental-fetch to reproduce browser streaming behavior.
- Inspect request headers for content-type and content-length mismatches.

Edge cases & gotchas:
- JSON-serializable prompts: pass arrays for multi-turn context rather than newline-joined strings to avoid prompt-injection formatting surprises.
- Token counting mismatch: local estimator vs backend counter can differ with special prefix tokens. For tight cost estimates use server-side token meta returned in response.
- Long-running KV-cache: when using stateful caching, confirm cache invalidation on model rollouts (pin versions or clear on deploy).

Testing recommendations:
- Add a small integration test in CI that calls the SDK against a mocked endpoint (wiremock/local stub). Keep it non-flaky: assert basic shape not content.
- Example jest test snippet (pseudo):
   jest.useFakeTimers();
   const mock = setupMockServer('/v1/generate', { body: { text: 'ok' } });
   const c = new Redwood({ baseUrl: mock.url, apiKey: 'test' });
   await expect(c.generate({ model: 'x', prompt: 'p' })).resolves.toHaveProperty('text');

Telemetry & observability notes (what to expect from SDK):
- SDK emits request-id and timing header (x-rw-req-id, x-rw-latency-ms). Surface those to logs for correlation with Console traces.
- Default telemetry is minimal; for prod, enable sdk telemetry hooks to capture token counts, latency, and model name.
- Privacy note: do not send PII in telemetry. Offer a sampling config for debug traces.

Production integration checklist (quick):
- Do not embed RW_API_KEY in client-side bundles. Use token exchange.
- Use exponential backoff for 429s and circuit-breaker for persistent failures.
- Configure model pinning in infra to avoid surprise model rollouts during canary.
- Add automated prompt-evals for critical flows to detect quality regressions after SDK or model changes.

Helpful CLI & debug commands:
- sdk-js doctor: quick local check for env, versions, and connectivity (TODO: implement as script)
- curl sanity check (above)
- node --trace-warnings index.js to catch unhandled promise rejections

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we add a tiny browser-first quickstart that uses ephemeral tokens + example serverless endpoint? (Maya to prototype)
- Add a small sandbox app (Next.js) demonstrating streaming UI + reconnects — low priority but high value for PD demos (Evan owns).
- Consider adding SDK lint rule for detecting accidental key-printers during build (strip process.env.RW_API_KEY leaks).

Related links / follow-ups:
- see linked PR for upcoming auth changes and new streaming API fields
- Confluence page for onramp flows (CONFLUENCE-DEVOPS-ONRAMP-912)
- Jira ticket: JIRA-ENG-3310 (add sdk doctor and integrate into quickstarts)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this page short. Point to full README for API details.
- Save 2 reusable snippets: minimal node, minimal react streaming. Put them in snippets/ so docs site can pull them.
- Reach out to platform infra about sample token endpoint for demos (avoid using permanent keys in samples).

End.
